question.title: Tokens in LLMs
question.scenario: A developer is working with a large language model API that charges based on tokens and has a maximum context window of 100,000 tokens.
question.question-text: In the context of large language models, what are tokens?

choices.choice: The basic units of text that the model processes, typically words or subwords
Memory units for storing model weights

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about what an LLM breaks text into before it can process anything — the smallest pieces it works with.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: In LLMs, tokens are the fundamental units of text that the model processes. A token might be a word, part of a word (subword), or a character. Tokenization converts text into these units before processing. LLM pricing is often based on tokens, and context windows (maximum input+output length) are measured in tokens. A typical rule of thumb is that 1 token is roughly 4 characters or 0.75 words in English.

ul.li: Different models use different tokenizers - the same text may result in different token counts.
Subword tokenization (like BPE) handles rare words by breaking them into common subunits.
Longer context windows allow more conversation history and larger documents but increase cost.
